newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia drags Finnish stocks after global turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Nokia drags Finnish stocks after global turmoil.

text.p: A sharp fall in bellwhether Nokia led the Helsinki bourse lower on Monday after Friday's global sell-off, but shares closed off lows as European markets recovered and Wall Street opened stronger, brokers said.

The HEX general index lost 0.99 percent to close at 2,446.8 points -- a fall which brokers said was about the equivalent of what other markets had lost since Thursday, when the Finnish bourse was last open for trade.

Friday was Finland's Independence Day holiday so shares escaped the worst of the turmoil that followed U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's warnings of "irrational exuberance" in financial markets.
Nokia fell 7.30 markka or almost three percent to close at 258.70, but ended well above its 254.20 markka session low.

Other shares held up better, with forestries bucking the trend to close higher on the back of Norway's Norske Skog's announcement that it expected pulp prices to rise at the start of 1997, and by Swedish Sodra's plan to hike pulp prices.

The forestry index was up 1.05 percent, with shares in Europe's largest forest industry firm UPM-Kymmene adding 0.70 markka to end at 94.00 markka. Enso rose 0.70 to 37.70 markka and Metsa-Serla added 0.50 markka to 34.00.
Brokers expected the market to recover on Tuesday as broad confidence returned to markets.
